Subject: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart & next steps

Hi Alex / Priya,

Great to meet earlier — thanks for the time and for walking through Acme's use case for native search and summarization in the Seller Portal. Per our call, summary + proposed next steps below.

Recap from the demo:
- You want a low-friction eval to validate latency and relevance on a 10k query test set, then a short PoC with 1k concurrent daily users.
- Data residency: U.S. only for PII flows.
- Security: SOC 2 evidence will be needed before any production purchase.
- Primary question for deployment mode: start with Hosted API for fast iteration vs Dedicated for predictable throughput and IP/data controls.

Recommended next steps (short-term eval path):
1) Quickstart on Hosted API — we can provision a temporary key and sample traffic runbook so your engineers can test with real load. This is fastest and keeps costs low during evaluation.
2) Run the 10k query test using our sample traffic (attached) to verify latency and token costs.
3) If throughput or data controls require it, we scope Dedicated capacity — we can provide an estimate in <48 hours.

I've attached: redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf (quickstart steps), redwood-eval-sample-traffic.jsonl (sample test traffic). Also linking the console quickstart: https://console.redwood.ai/quickstart?token=abc123

Questions / asks for you:
- Can you share the PII flow list so we can confirm U.S. region-only routing?
- Do you want us to pre-schedule a Dedicated scoping call or start only on Hosted?

I'll send temporary quickstart credentials once you confirm.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Hosted API evaluation — quickstart & next steps

Hi Alex — great questions, and thanks for the security questionnaire — we can start the quickstart while we triage the questionnaire. Answers below and next steps.

1) Data residency on Hosted API:
- Hosted API supports region pinning at the account/token level for most customers; we can route requests to our U.S. region only for your evaluation (and for production if needed).
- For regulated workflows that require customer-managed networking or air-gapped environments, our Private (VPC/on-prem) option is available but is usually a later step.

2) Rate limits / throughput (Hosted):
- Default tier: 60 requests/minute (rps-based limits apply for streaming endpoints).
- For PoC customers we can temporarily increase limits to accommodate bursts — e.g., short-term burst to ~200 qps for load tests when coordinated with our infra team. Sustained throughput for Hosted depends on plan; if you need predictable capacity and SLA-backed throughput we recommend Dedicated, which we can size after seeing sample traffic.
- Primary levers: batching, KV caching, and prefix caching — these reduce token throughput and improve unit cost. We'll include suggested batching configs in the quickstart doc.

3) Security artifacts:
- Attaching our SOC 2 summary and SOC 2 audit contact in the console link. We'll also provide a redacted architecture diagram and data flow mapping after we review your questionnaire.

Next steps (what I'll do):
- Provision a temporary Hosted API key and add you to a U.S-only account. Link to quickstart + temp key will be shared via console (https://console.redwood.ai/quickstart?token=abc123).
- Upload the sample traffic and run a load test with Redwood infra to validate the burst to 200 qps; I will schedule the load test window with your engineering team.
- Share SOC2 summary and a short readout doc (attaching redwood-hosted-quickstart.pdf now).

What I need from you:
- Confirm a 2-hour window next week to run the burst test (we recommend Tue or Wed morning PST).
- Share the list of PII fields and an example payload so we can validate routing and masking options.

If you confirm the above, I'll also open a HubSpot deal and send a short MSA draft for e-sign if you want to fast-track Dedicated pricing later.

Thanks,
Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
